cards.explanation: The answer is Love. Paul puts it plainly: "Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up." Love is the one doing the building. Knowledge is not a bad thing, friends, but it can swell your head like dough with too much air in it. Love is what actually makes something solid.

The answer is that the person is known by God. Paul says, "But the one who loves God is known by God." Notice he doesn't brag about what the person knows. He talks about who knows the person. Being known by God is bigger than any pile of facts in your head.

The answer is False. Paul says, "We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world…" He adds that there is no God but one (1 Corinthians 8:4). So no idol is a real power, however fancy it looks. A statue can have the best paint job in town and still be nothing at all in the world.

The answer is Jesus Christ. Paul says, "…there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist." One God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ. Many things in the world get called lords, but Paul names only one Lord for us. That's a short list, friends, and I love it.

The answer is True. Paul says there is "…one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist." All things came from the Father, and all things came through Jesus Christ. Same all things, both of them in the picture. That's a lot of things, and I've got a bakery to run.

The answer is that they eat it as if it were sacrificed to an idol. Paul says some people "…are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol." For them it still feels tied to the idol. Their habits haven't caught up with what others know. Paul adds that since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.

The answer is False. Paul calls their conscience weak. He says they are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled. Weak is the word, friends, and he doesn't soften it.

The answer is False. Paul says, "But food does not bring us closer to God…" He adds that we are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do. So the plate is not where the nearness to God happens.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak." Having freedom is one thing. Watching where you swing it is another. I once swung my mustache around a crowded counter, and let's just say my cookie cutter kids learned to duck.

The answer is False. Paul asks, "…will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?" The one with a weak conscience sees a well-informed believer eating and is encouraged to eat too, not to stay away. That's the danger, friends. Watching somebody can nudge a person in the wrong direction.

The answer is the knowledge of the well-informed. Paul says it straight: "…this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge." The knowledge itself is not the problem. It's what happens when it's used without love, since Paul says love is what builds up (1 Corinthians 8:1). This is a heavy part.

The answer is Christ. Paul says, "…you sin against Christ." He also calls the weak brother one "…for whom Christ died…" So wounding a weak conscience is not only a squabble between two people. Paul says it is sinning against Christ.

The answer is that he will never eat meat again. Paul says, "…I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble." That's him giving up something he has every right to eat. He doesn't ask the brother to change first. I'd call that love building up, friends.
